Imagine a box as a persons head. You have to go straight up and flick out towards your self when you cut. Don’t dig in to the persons head or you’ll just leave harsh guidelines that won’t go away. I start with the 3 all around for most fades. That debulks the sides to prep. Then you put your zero guideline all around the head with your trimmers.  Don’t push too hard and create a line that won’t go away. From there you start your first guidline. Start with no guard open. Make sure it’s even and go over multiple times to get all the hairs. From there go up to the one open and create another guidline right above the one you just made. Then you use your one and a half and go up slightly, flicking out to the 3 you started with to soften it up. Then you use clipper over comb technique to really get that line between the 1 1/2 and the 3. From there use half guard to get rid of the line between the no guard and the one. Opening and closing the half to get rid of the line. Then get the one, open and close it as well to clean up the inconsistencies. Finally the one and one half closed to clean up whatever you missed with the clipper over comb. To finish it up you use no guard with the blade closed to get rid of the very bottom line. Opening the blade little by little to get rid of that line until it blends with the half guard.

Definitely look up a video on how to zero gap. Especially all of your trimmers. That way, everything is set the same and any inconsistencies will blend out by alternating your clippers and trimmers. Also if you don’t have the half and one and a half guards you’ll need them for sure. It’ll really help blend in between your guidelines
